note.question: How should a manufacturer and retailer jointly adapt quality, wholesale price, and retail price when consumers underreact to right-hand price digits, and when does 99-ending rigidity worsen or alleviate double marginalization?
note.overview: A manufacturer strategically chooses product quality and a wholesale price while anticipating a retailer's retail-price best response. The paper solves this sequential vertical-channel game by backward induction and characterizes how consumer left-digit bias changes price-point equilibria, double marginalization, quality, profits, and welfare.

components.label: Solution or estimation method
components.explanation: The paper embeds a discontinuous perceived-price map in a vertically differentiated demand model, solves centralized pricing and quality benchmarks, solves the manufacturer-retailer game by backward induction across interior and 99-ending regimes, and compares profits, quality, prices, coordination, and consumer surplus through analytical thresholds and numerical illustrations.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: The manufacturer first chooses product quality q and wholesale price w. Observing these choices, the retailer chooses the posted retail price p, represented by a left block n and right digits Delta. Consumers then decide whether to buy from their perceived price and quality. The manufacturer anticipates the retailer's best response, and the equilibrium is solved by backward induction.

components.label: Backward-induction equilibrium of the manufacturer-retailer channel
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Backward-induction equilibrium of the manufacturer-retailer channel. Section 6 states that the decentralized channel is analyzed by backward induction. Lemma 3 derives manufacturer wholesale-price and retailer retail-price outcomes conditional on quality, Lemma 4 adds endogenous manufacturer quality, and Proposition 3 identifies the empirically relevant region in which 99-ending pricing is the only equilibrium and both channel members gain relative to rational demand.
